attributes.provenance: src/game/sfx/psfx.c::fn_80089350, the p+284/field_11C conversion (worktree GDL-Claude-PsfxDefake, work_claim.psfx-defake.20260830.v1); attempt.psfx-defakematch-tupass-w2.20260830.v1
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies when the SAME field is dereferenced through a stationary base pointer (a function parameter or other already-resident register, not a walked/indexed address) at two or more WIDELY SEPARATED points in a large, already register-tuned function.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast establishes that REPEATED casts of the same field regress and a declared-once alias fixes it; this is a distinct, narrower failure that neither that law nor claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing predicts. In fn_80089350 (`u8* p` parameter, not walked or indexed), converting `*(u32*)(p + 284) & 0xFFB7FFFF` (an early, register-light region) to `((Player*)p)->field_11C & 0xFFB7FFFF` was completely neutral (real unchanged). Converting the SECOND, unrelated occurrence of the identical field 80+ lines later -- `*(u32*)(p + 284) & 0x00100000` inside `if (n > 0 && ...)`, positioned right after a dense missile-fan loop with heavy Effects-array/pmissile_sfxidx pressure -- regressed real 127->337 (insns 355/354->355/356) EVEN THOUGH the first site's conversion was kept and proven neutral. This is not the declared-alias law's 'repeated inline cast' failure mode (there were only 2 occurrences total, 80 lines apart, not 3+ adjacent); it is also not a signedness issue (an explicit `(u32)` cast matching the original load type produced the identical regression, real 337, byte-for-byte). The two sites are register-pressure-independent in the C source but NOT in MWCC's register allocator: the second site sits in a region where the allocator is already near-saturated from unrelated nearby code, and materializing `p`'s field-access address a second way (even via the exact same struct-typed expression already proven safe elsewhere) perturbs that local allocation enough to cascade through the remainder of the function. Consequence: when a field conversion is safe at one occurrence, DO NOT assume it transfers to a second, distant occurrence of the same field in the same function, especially inside or just after a loop/dense-computation region -- gate every occurrence independently, and if a later occurrence regresses, leave that ONE site raw (partial conversion, matching the project's established partial-conversion idiom) rather than reverting the whole field or hunting for an alternate typed-alias form (an alias was not tried here specifically, but the identical-shape-cast negative result and the position-correlation with a dense preceding region both point at allocator pressure, not expression form, as the cause).
